title: Prove an operand-preserving eight-tape multiplier with paid copying and head return
body:
The concrete multiplier now retains both original operand words while producing the exact padded double-width product. One fixed finite eight-tape program handles every supplied a,b<2^n, including width zero, genuinely halts, returns all eight heads to physical zero, and leaves its five other work tapes globally blank within 280*n^2+284*n+74 transitions. A real three-state paired copier costs exactly2*n+2; the scheduler handoff costs1; the existing origin-return core costs at most280*n^2+282*n+71. No size register, hypothetical copier or free head reset is used.

Applications prove actual minimal-width natural runs and arbitrary finite-bank host calls. Extra host spectators retain their entire head/cell functions at every prefix. Protected source heads move during copying; their stationary-prefix preservation theorem begins at the actual arithmetic core boundary. Literal original word equality includes the full owned tapes. Supplied padding remains an explicit input convention, not a paid parser.

Validation: all four new modules and aggregator received fresh independent Lean4.34.1 kernel checks, followed by an unchanged frozen universal-root kernel/axiom check and a complete fresh audit of 5,115 declarations (2,638 theorems). Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are admitted. Four actual Lean ownership/axiom fixtures,11 audit-report corruption controls,1365 exhaustive paired-copy word pairs,six seeded long cases and six rejecting table mutations passed.59 unchanged dependency artifacts were reused under exact prior verified source/artifact/import/toolchain/revision guards with the two-generation audit chain independently checked. Local verification is not a full cold rebuild of those59; public replay.py supports full cold source rebuild. Mathlib cache binaries are pinned, not independently rebuilt. Hosted CI and human review are not claimed.

Actual upstream main refreshed to6ca6f217708b075814de409ad693fea9a2aaa760, with a bounded recent-PR inventory through2780. This extends the actual PR2780 origin-return predecessor. PR2776 already implements source-preserving copying and paid rewinds in its ordered-shear controller. Dan Brown and Kenny Daniel's external finite-TM2 development already proves asymptotic multiplication; its prior pinned source review is credited, not independently replayed. The contribution is this particular complete eight-tape multiplication ABI and charged certificate, not first multiplication/copying, a new exponent or selected kappa. No external platypii source is copied/imported. Retained source licenses and notices remain.

Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, one root and three parallel agents. Open next questions are charged parsing and actual recursive marked-buffer caller integration. No public repository was modified by this work.
